claims.text: The material is HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure.
The proposed simulations integrate machine-learning potentials trained on DFT data.
The intervention will improve the predictive accuracy of Young’s modulus by at least 15% relative to established simulations.
The intervention will improve the predictive accuracy of yield strength by at least 15% relative to established simulations.
The intervention will improve prediction of fracture-related behavior by at least 15% relative to established simulations.
The intervention will reduce computational time by at least 30% relative to established simulations.
Machine-learning potentials trained on DFT data model atomic interactions more accurately than established simulations.
More accurate modeling of atomic interactions will improve prediction of the alloy’s mechanical and fracture behavior.
The hypothesis may fail if the machine-learning potentials do not capture the complex interactions in the hierarchical heterostructure.
The hypothesis may fail if the DFT training data do not represent behavior under tensile and fracture-testing conditions.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% predictive-accuracy improvement is declared to falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain at least a 25% reduction in computational time is declared to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis claims minimum gains of 15% in accuracy and 30% in computational time, but the falsification rule uses weaker thresholds of 10% and 25%. Results such as 12% accuracy improvement and 27% time reduction would violate the hypothesis while not satisfying its stated falsification rule.
Computational time is part of the falsification rule but is omitted from the declared measurement list.
